text:
maria.dev: FYI customer 'payrollly' opened an escalation — their Node TS integration is intermittently getting 502s and long tail latencies when calling our /v1/generate endpoint. They say retries are firing and sometimes duplicate POSTs hit the backend. Repro steps below.

maria.dev: package.json: 
```json
{
  "name": "payrollly",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "^1.4.2",
    "undici": "^5.0.0"
  }
}
```

maria.dev: client code (small):
```ts
const sdk = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await sdk.generate({ model: 'gpt-neo-3', prompt: '...' });
```

maria.dev: They assert they use an AbortController timeout per-request. Behavior: if the request times out client-side, SDK retries, but the original request is still processed server-side -> sometimes causes duplicate side-effects. Logs attached by customer show repeated attempts without a clear abort event.

sam.sre: Can you paste the raw request/response log? Also confirm Node version (18 vs 20) and undici exact subversion. undici v5 changed Signal semantics.

maria.dev: Node 18.17.1 (customer). undici@5.12.0. SDK 1.4.2. Excerpt from client log (timestamps redacted):

```
[attempt 0] POST /v1/generate 502 (body: "Bad Gateway")
[attempt 1] POST /v1/generate 502
[attempt 2] POST /v1/generate aborted? no signal fired, downstream started processing request id=abc123
```

maria.dev: They also showed server logs where processing time continued after client timeout (so backend is executing). Customer worried about idempotency/duplicate charges.

kevin.support: Important detail — POST endpoints must be treated as non-idempotent by default. If users rely on client-side retries, they need idempotency keys or server-side dedupe. Short term, tell customer to set maxRetries=0 or add Idempotency-Key. We should recommend SDK default to safer behavior.

olga.eng: This looks like undici's abort propagation edge-case. In undici v5 some AbortSignal behaviors changed: aborting the fetch doesn't always cancel the in-flight request when pipelining/keepalive is involved. SDK currently calls fetch with the provided AbortSignal and then does a retry on network errors — we might not be forcing a hard socket destroy.

deploy-bot: deploy bot: released sdk@1.4.2 to production at 2024-08-02T14:12:07Z :rocket:

support-engineer: For reproducing: enable undici debug logs: set UNDICI_DEBUG=1 on the client process and capture the socket lifecycle. Also capture request-id header from our API responses (x-redwood-request-id) so we can correlate server handling.

maria.dev: Customer provided curl repro that shows duplicated server-side work when client uses a short timeout and retries via SDK: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'Idempotency-Key:' -d '{"prompt":"..."}' --max-time 2
```

maria.dev: If they remove undici and use node-fetch (older behavior), they don't see duplicates. So it's likely a change in undici + Node 18 runtime.

sam.sre: Short-term recommendations to give customer: 
- Add an Idempotency-Key for POSTs that mutate state.
- Set SDK retry settings to 0 or 1 and increase client timeout a bit. Example: 
```ts
const sdk = new RedwoodClient({
  retry: { maxRetries: 0 }
});
```
- Alternatively, wrap request in an AbortController and ensure you call controller.abort() on timeout, but note that undici v5 may not always close the socket immediately.

kevin.support: We should ship an SDK patch that: 
- ensures underlying socket is destroyed when AbortSignal fires (best-effort), 
- expose a safer default for retries on non-idempotent methods, 
- add telemetry header to correlate retries (x-redwood-retry-index).

olga.eng: Agreed. Quick patch idea: on abort, call res.socket?.destroy() (guarded) for undici, and ensure we clear any pending retry timers. Also add docs about undici versions. I'll open a PR.

support-engineer: Also ask the customer to run with UNDICI_DEBUG=1 and provide a snippet of the raw TCP/HTTP lifecycle. Capture x-redwood-request-id values from server so we can tell which attempts were processed.

maria.dev: Customer asked whether they should downgrade undici to v4 as a temporary mitigation. Thoughts?

sam.sre: Downgrading may avoid the signal semantics change but could introduce other bugs. If they can add Idempotency-Key that's safest. If they absolutely must, try undici@4.x in a staging env and see if the duplicate behavior stops.

kevin.support: I'll draft a customer-facing note: explain risk of duplicates on non-idempotent POSTs, show immediate mitigation (idempotency key / disable retries), and promise a fix ETA.

maria.dev: Customer wants ETA. Any timeline?

olga.eng: I can prioritize a small SDK patch to 1) better destroy sockets on abort and 2) add x-redwood-retry-index header. Target: PR today, release 1.4.3 early next week if tests pass. Will update this thread with PR link. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria.dev: Thanks — I'll relay workaround and ask them to capture UNDICI_DEBUG logs and request IDs.

support-engineer: Tagging follow-up checklist: 
- collect client UNDICI_DEBUG logs, Node version, undici version
- collect x-redwood-request-id for processed attempts
- note whether request method is POST and whether Idempotency-Key provided
- record SDK retry config

maria.dev: Copy that. I'll push a support ticket to the customer with the suggested mitigations.

kevin.support: Also file a product issue: make safer default retries for POSTs (opt-in for aggressive retries).

olga.eng: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 (WIP) — implements socket destroy on abort + adds retry-index header. Will post CI results.

maria.dev: :thumbsup: closing loop with customer after they share logs.
